learn.rule: A paragraph has one topic sentence that tells the big idea. Every detail sentence must help explain that idea.
learn.ruleEs: Un párrafo tiene una oración temática que dice la idea principal. Cada oración de detalle debe ayudar a explicar esa idea.
learn.model: Rivers slowly change the land around them. Moving water carries soil and small rocks away from the banks.
learn.notice: Read the first sentence. It names the big idea. Then check that the next sentence is a detail about that idea.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best topic sentence for these details?
items.text: Moving water carries away soil and small rocks. Over many years, a river can cut a deep canyon. The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon.

options.text: The Colorado River is a famous river.
Rivers slowly change the land around them.
Canyons are fun places to visit.

items.why: A topic sentence covers all of the details. Choice A is only about one river, and choice C is about something the details never mention.
items.whyEs: Una oración temática cubre todos los detalles. La opción A habla de un solo río, y la opción C trata de algo que los detalles nunca mencionan.

items.prompt: Check every detail that belongs in a paragraph about how rivers change the land.

options.text: Fast water pulls sand and soil from the riverbank.
My cousin bought a new fishing rod last week.
Over thousands of years, a river can carve a wide valley.
Many deserts get very little rain each year.
Soil dropped at a river's mouth can build a flat delta.

items.why: Details must explain the topic sentence. The three correct sentences each show one way a river changes the land. The other two are about different topics.
items.whyEs: Los detalles deben explicar la oración temática. Las tres oraciones correctas muestran una manera en que un río cambia la tierra. Las otras dos son de otros temas.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that introduces an example.
parts: , the Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon over millions of years.
items.model: Rivers change the land. For example, the Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon over millions of years.
items.why: The second sentence gives one real example of the big idea, so For example is the signal that fits. However shows a contrast, and Finally shows the last step.
items.whyEs: La segunda oración da un ejemplo real de la idea principal, así que For example es la señal correcta. However muestra un contraste y Finally muestra el último paso.

items.prompt: Put the sentences in order to make a clear paragraph.
lines: Rivers change the land in several ways.
First, fast water pulls soil and small rocks from the banks.
Next, the river carries this material downstream.
Finally, the river drops it where the water slows down, and new land builds up.
items.why: The topic sentence comes first. Then the signal words First, Next, and Finally put the details in the order they happen.
items.whyEs: La oración temática va primero. Luego las señales First, Next y Finally ponen los detalles en el orden en que ocurren.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence is neither too big nor too small for these details?
items.text: Sand and soil settle where a river slows down. A delta is a fan of new land at a river's mouth. The Mississippi River built a large delta at the Gulf of Mexico.

options.text: Earth has many kinds of land.
The Mississippi River is long.
Deltas are new land built from the soil a river drops.

items.why: A topic sentence should be just the right size. Choice A is too big because it covers all land, and choice B is too small and does not match the details.
items.whyEs: Una oración temática debe tener el tamaño justo. La opción A es demasiado grande porque abarca toda la tierra, y la opción B es demasiado pequeña y no coincide con los detalles.

items.prompt: Which closing sentence best finishes this paragraph?
items.text: Rivers slowly change the land around them. Water pulls sand from the riverbank and carries it downstream. Over thousands of years, a river can cut a deep valley. Where a river slows near the sea, it drops soil and builds a delta.

options.text: Many people enjoy swimming in rivers on hot days.
In short, rivers are powerful forces that carve and build land.
Next, I will write about lakes.

items.why: A closing sentence brings the big idea back in new words. Choice A starts a new idea, and choice C only announces what comes next.
items.whyEs: Una oración de cierre retoma la idea principal con otras palabras. La opción A empieza una idea nueva y la opción C solo anuncia lo que sigue.

write.prompt: Write a topic sentence and two detail sentences about forests. Use a signal word in each detail.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración temática y dos oraciones de detalle sobre los bosques. Usa una palabra de señal en cada detalle.
write.frame: Forests help animals live. For example, ___. Another detail is that ___.

label: I used a signal word like for example, also, or another
Usé una palabra de señal como for example, also o another

write.model: Forests help animals live. For example, trees give birds a safe place to build nests. Another detail is that fallen logs shelter insects, frogs, and mice.

familyTalk.en: At dinner, name one big idea, such as 'Our neighborhood is a good place to live,' and give two details that prove it.
familyTalk.es: En la cena, digan una idea grande, como 'Nuestro barrio es un buen lugar para vivir', y den dos detalles que lo prueben.

teacherTip.en: Cover the topic sentence of a model paragraph and ask pairs to write one that fits every detail before revealing the original.
teacherTip.es: Tapa la oración temática de un párrafo modelo y pide que las parejas escriban una que encaje con todos los detalles antes de mostrar la original.

learn.rule: The topic sentence tells the big idea. Each detail sentence gives a fact that belongs to that idea.
learn.ruleEs: La oración temática dice la idea principal. Cada oración de detalle da un dato que pertenece a esa idea.
learn.model: The Nile River was the lifeline of ancient Egypt. Every year, its flood left rich black soil on the farmland.
learn.notice: The first sentence is big. The second sentence is smaller and gives one fact about the Nile.

items.prompt: Pick the topic sentence that matches all three details.
items.text: Farmers grew wheat and barley in the rich soil. Boats carried people and goods up and down the river. Reeds called papyrus grew along the banks and became writing sheets.

options.text: The Nile River gave ancient Egyptians food, travel, and writing materials.
The ancient Egyptians built the Great Pyramid of Giza.
Papyrus is a tall plant that grows near water.

items.why: The topic sentence has to cover food, travel, and writing. Choice B is a different topic, and choice C covers only one detail.
items.whyEs: La oración temática debe cubrir la comida, los viajes y la escritura. La opción B es otro tema y la opción C cubre solo un detalle.

items.prompt: Check every detail that belongs in a paragraph about how ancient Egyptians used the Nile.

options.text: Camels are well suited to desert travel.
Each summer, floodwater spread rich soil over the farmland.
Many people today visit museums to see mummies.
Boats with sails carried grain and stone along the river.
Egyptians pressed papyrus reeds into sheets to write on.

items.why: A detail belongs only if it shows how people used the Nile. The correct choices show farming, travel, and writing. The others are about camels and museums.
items.whyEs: Un detalle pertenece solo si muestra cómo la gente usaba el Nilo. Las opciones correctas muestran la agricultura, el transporte y la escritura. Las otras tratan de camellos y museos.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that adds one more detail.
parts: Farmers grew wheat and barley in the river's rich soil.
, boats on the Nile carried grain and stone to faraway cities.
items.model: Farmers grew wheat and barley in the river's rich soil. Also, boats on the Nile carried grain and stone to faraway cities.
items.why: The second sentence adds another way the Nile helped Egypt, so Also fits. But and Instead would show a contrast that is not in these sentences.
items.whyEs: La segunda oración añade otra manera en que el Nilo ayudó a Egipto, así que Also es la correcta. But e Instead mostrarían un contraste que no está en estas oraciones.

items.prompt: Put the paragraph in order, starting with the topic sentence.
lines: The yearly Nile flood helped Egyptian farmers grow food.
First, heavy rains far to the south made the river rise each summer.
Next, the floodwater spread over the fields and left rich black soil.
Finally, when the water went down, farmers planted their seeds.
items.why: The topic sentence gives the big idea. Then First, Next, and Finally show the steps of the flood in the order they happened.
items.whyEs: La oración temática da la idea principal. Luego First, Next y Finally muestran los pasos de la inundación en el orden en que ocurrieron.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence fits these details without being too big or too small?
items.text: Egyptians pressed papyrus reeds into flat sheets. They wrote on the sheets with reed pens and ink. Scribes used papyrus to record taxes and stories.

options.text: Writing has been used by people all over the world.
Scribes wrote about taxes.
Papyrus was an important writing material in ancient Egypt.

items.why: Choice C names the paper-like sheets that every detail talks about. Choice A is too big, and choice B leaves out how papyrus was made.
items.whyEs: La opción C nombra las hojas de papiro de las que habla cada detalle. La opción A es demasiado grande y la B deja fuera cómo se hacía el papiro.

items.prompt: Which concluding sentence best ends this paragraph?
items.text: The Nile River was the heart of ancient Egypt. Its yearly flood left rich soil, so farmers grew plenty of food. Boats carried people and goods from town to town. Reeds along the banks became papyrus for writing.

options.text: Ancient Egypt also had huge stone temples.
I will tell you about pyramids next.
In short, the Nile gave ancient Egypt the food, travel, and writing sheets it needed.

items.why: A concluding sentence restates the big idea in new words. Choice A adds a new topic, and choice B only announces what comes next.
items.whyEs: Una oración de conclusión repite la idea principal con otras palabras. La opción A añade un tema nuevo y la opción B solo anuncia lo que sigue.

write.prompt: Write a topic sentence and two detail sentences about how rivers help people. Use a signal word in each detail.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración temática y dos oraciones de detalle sobre cómo los ríos ayudan a las personas. Usa una palabra de señal en cada detalle.
write.text: Topic: Rivers helped early towns grow.
write.frame: Rivers helped early towns grow. For example, ___. Also, ___.

label: I used a signal word like for example, also, or another
Usé una palabra de señal como for example, also o another

write.model: Rivers helped early towns grow. For example, people used river water to grow crops and give animals a drink. Also, boats carried food and tools from town to town.

familyTalk.en: Ask your child to explain a big idea about your city or town and then give two true details that support it.
familyTalk.es: Pidan a su hijo o hija que explique una idea grande sobre su ciudad o pueblo y luego dé dos detalles verdaderos que la apoyen.

teacherTip.en: Have students underline the topic sentence and number each detail, then cross out any sentence that does not explain the big idea.
teacherTip.es: Pide que los estudiantes subrayen la oración temática y numeren cada detalle, y luego tachen cualquier oración que no explique la idea principal.

sets.title: Sleep Powers Your Body
sets.titleEs: El sueño da energía a tu cuerpo

learn.rule: Start with a topic sentence, then add details that all belong. A closing sentence can bring the big idea back.
learn.ruleEs: Empieza con una oración temática y añade detalles que pertenezcan. Una oración de cierre puede retomar la idea principal.
learn.model: Sleep keeps your body and mind healthy. While you sleep, your body grows and repairs itself.
learn.notice: The topic sentence names sleep and health. The detail tells one thing your body does while you sleep.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the strongest topic sentence for these details?
items.text: Your brain stores what you learned during the day. Your muscles and bones grow while you rest. You feel calmer and more focused after a good night's sleep.

options.text: Eating breakfast gives you energy for the day.
Your brain stores memories while you sleep.
Sleep helps your brain and body in many ways.

items.why: The topic sentence must cover the brain, the body, and your mood. Choice A is about breakfast, and choice B covers only the brain.
items.whyEs: La oración temática debe cubrir el cerebro, el cuerpo y el ánimo. La opción A trata del desayuno y la opción B cubre solo el cerebro.

items.prompt: Check every detail that belongs in a paragraph about why sleep is important.

options.text: Sleep helps your brain remember what you learned.
Sleeping well can lift your mood.
Many people eat cereal for breakfast.
Rested students can focus better in class.
Drinking water helps your body stay cool.

items.why: Each correct detail tells one way that sleep helps you. The cereal and water sentences are about other healthy habits, so they do not support this topic.
items.whyEs: Cada detalle correcto dice una manera en que dormir te ayuda. Las oraciones sobre el cereal y el agua tratan de otros hábitos saludables, así que no apoyan este tema.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that shows a result.
parts: Screens can make it hard to fall asleep.
, many doctors suggest turning them off an hour before bedtime.
items.model: Screens can make it hard to fall asleep. As a result, many doctors suggest turning them off an hour before bedtime.
items.why: The second sentence is the result of the first one, so As a result fits. However would show a surprise, and For example would start an example.
items.whyEs: La segunda oración es el resultado de la primera, así que As a result es la correcta. However mostraría una sorpresa y For example empezaría un ejemplo.

items.prompt: Put the sentences in order to build a paragraph.
lines: A good bedtime routine helps you fall asleep.
First, turn off screens and dim the lights.
Next, brush your teeth and put on pajamas.
Finally, read a quiet book until you feel sleepy.
items.why: The topic sentence tells the big idea. The signal words First, Next, and Finally put the routine in a clear order.
items.whyEs: La oración temática dice la idea principal. Las señales First, Next y Finally ponen la rutina en un orden claro.

items.prompt: Which topic sentence is the right size for these details?
items.text: A steady bedtime teaches your body when to feel sleepy. Waking at the same time each day makes mornings easier. Regular sleep times help you get the rest you need.

options.text: Health is important for everyone.
Regular sleep times help your body get the rest it needs.
Mornings can be busy.

items.why: Choice B matches every detail about sleep times. Choice A is too big, and choice C is about a different idea.
items.whyEs: La opción B coincide con todos los detalles sobre los horarios de sueño. La opción A es demasiado grande y la C trata de otra idea.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best closing sentence for this paragraph?
items.text: Sleep is important for growing students. Your brain stores new learning while you rest. Your body repairs itself and grows stronger. A good night's sleep also lifts your mood.

options.text: In short, enough sleep helps students learn, grow, and feel good.
Some students stay up late on weekends.
Tomorrow I will explain how to cook dinner.

items.why: A closing sentence restates the big idea in fresh words. Choice B is a new fact, and choice C moves to a different topic.
items.whyEs: Una oración de cierre repite la idea principal con palabras nuevas. La opción B es un dato nuevo y la opción C pasa a otro tema.

write.prompt: Write a topic sentence and two detail sentences about exercise. Use a signal word in each detail.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración temática y dos oraciones de detalle sobre el ejercicio. Usa una palabra de señal en cada detalle.
write.text: Topic: Exercise keeps your body strong.
write.frame: Exercise keeps your body strong. For example, ___. Also, ___.

label: I used a signal word like for example, also, or another
Usé una palabra de señal como for example, also o another

write.model: Exercise keeps your body strong. For example, running makes your heart and leg muscles stronger. Also, playing sports helps you sleep well and feel happy.

familyTalk.en: Before bed, say a healthy habit as a big idea and give two reasons it helps you.
familyTalk.es: Antes de dormir, digan un hábito saludable como idea grande y den dos razones por las que les ayuda.

teacherTip.en: Give each pair a cut-up paragraph with one off-topic sentence mixed in and ask them to find it and explain why it does not belong.
teacherTip.es: Da a cada pareja un párrafo recortado con una oración fuera de tema mezclada y pide que la encuentren y expliquen por qué no pertenece.
